subproblems.title: The coordinate covector e_j ⌟ det on ℝ^{m+1} and its values on the basis with one vector removed
subproblems.statement: For every m ∈ ℕ and j ∈ Fin (m+1) there is a continuous alternating m-linear form β on ℝ^{m+1} (β ∈ Covector (Euclid (m+1)) m) such that, for every i ∈ Fin (m+1), β evaluated on the standard basis family (e₀, …, e_m) of ℝ^{m+1} with e_i removed (Fin.removeNth i) equals (−1)^j if i = j and 0 if i ≠ j. Source: step 2 of the parent proof (the constant covector βⱼ(w₁,…,w_m) := δ(eⱼ, w₁, …, w_m)), extracted as a stand-alone lemma.
Notation: ℝ^p means Euclid p = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p); e_l := EuclideanSpace.single l (1 : ℝ) is the l-th standard basis vector; for an (m+1)-tuple w, removeNth i w := Fin.removeNth i w is the m-tuple with entry i deleted, so (removeNth i w)(l) = w(i.succAbove l) (Fin.removeNth_apply); Covector E m = E [⋀^Fin m]→L[ℝ] ℝ (continuous alternating m-linear forms); DifferentialForm E m = E → Covector E m; exteriorDerivative = Mathlib's extDeriv (Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter06.exteriorDerivative is an abbrev), with the alternating-sum formula dω(x)(w₀,…,w_m) = Σᵢ (−1)^i • D[y ↦ ω(y)(removeNth i w)](x)(wᵢ) for ω differentiable at x (exteriorDerivative_apply); IsSmoothForm ψ := ContDiff ℝ ∞ ψ where ∞ = ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) (in the frozen contract scope `∞` denotes ENNReal's ∞ because of `open scoped ENNReal`, so write the order as (⊤ : ℕ∞)).
1. Let b := (EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin (m+1)) ℝ).toBasis, the standard basis of ℝ^{m+1}; b l = e_l for every l (OrthonormalBasis.coe_toBasis, EuclideanSpace.basisFun_apply; `funext l; simp [b]`). Let δ₀ := b.det, the determinant alternating (m+1)-linear map with respect to b (Module.Basis.det). By Module.Basis.det_apply, δ₀ c = det (b.toMatrix c), and b.toMatrix c is the matrix whose (r, l)-entry is b.repr (c l) r = (c l) r. Hence δ₀ c = det (Matrix.of fun r l => c l r) for every c : Fin (m+1) → ℝ^{m+1} (in Lean, after `rw [Module.Basis.det_apply]` the goal is closed by `congr 1`).
2. Continuity of δ₀. The map c ↦ Matrix.of (fun r l => c l r) is continuous, because each entry c ↦ (c l) r is the composition of the evaluation c ↦ c l (continuous_apply l) with the continuous coordinate projection EuclideanSpace.proj r, and a matrix-valued map with continuous entries is continuous (continuous_matrix). Composing with the determinant (Continuous.matrix_det) shows that c ↦ δ₀ c is continuous by step 1. (The automatic-continuity lemma MultilinearMap.continuous_of_finiteDimensional is not available in the import closure, so this explicit argument is used.)
3. Consequently δ₀ underlies a continuous alternating map δ ∈ Covector (Euclid (m+1)) (m+1) with δ c = δ₀ c for every c (in Lean: `let δ : Covector (Euclid (m + 1)) (m + 1) := { b.det with cont := hcont }`; then `δ c = b.det c` holds by rfl).
4. Define β := δ.curryLeft (b j) ∈ Covector (Euclid (m+1)) m (ContinuousAlternatingMap.curryLeft). By ContinuousAlternatingMap.curryLeft_apply_apply, β w = δ (Matrix.vecCons (b j) w) = δ₀ (Matrix.vecCons (b j) w) for every w : Fin m → ℝ^{m+1}. Since (l ↦ e_l) = b (step 1), the claim for a fixed i reads δ₀ c_i = (if i = j then (−1)^j else 0), where c_i := Matrix.vecCons (b j) (removeNth i b) (Matrix.vecCons = Fin.cons). Split on whether i = j.
5. Case i = j. By Fin.cons_removeNth_eq_comp_cycleRange_symm (with x := b and p := i), c_i = Fin.cons (b i) (removeNth i b) = b ∘ σ with σ := (Fin.cycleRange i).symm. By AlternatingMap.map_perm, δ₀ (b ∘ σ) = sign σ • δ₀ b. Here δ₀ b = b.det b = 1 (Module.Basis.det_self) and sign σ = sign (cycleRange i) (Equiv.Perm.sign_symm) = (−1)^i in ℤˣ (Fin.sign_cycleRange). Hence δ₀ c_i = ((−1)^i : ℤˣ) • (1 : ℝ) = (−1 : ℝ)^i (`simp [Units.smul_def]`), which is (−1)^j because i = j.
6. Case i ≠ j. As j ≠ i, Fin.exists_succAbove_eq gives l ∈ Fin m with i.succAbove l = j. Then c_i 0 = b j and c_i (l.succ) = (removeNth i b) l = b (i.succAbove l) = b j (Fin.removeNth_apply), while 0 ≠ l.succ (Fin.succ_ne_zero). An alternating map vanishes on a family with equal entries at two distinct indices (AlternatingMap.map_eq_zero_of_eq, applied with indices 0 and l.succ; the entry equality is closed by `simp [Fin.removeNth_apply, hl]`), so δ₀ c_i = 0.
7. Steps 5 and 6 give β (removeNth i (l ↦ e_l)) = if i = j then (−1)^j else 0 for every i ∈ Fin (m+1) (`split_ifs`), so β has the required property. (For m = 0 the same argument applies verbatim: β is the 0-covector with value δ₀(e₀) = 1 = (−1)^0.) ∎

Notation. P := n + 1 + k; ℝ^d := Euclid d; e_j := EuclideanSpace.single j (1 : ℝ) ∈ ℝ^{n+1}, e := (e_0, …, e_n), and removeNth i e := Fin.removeNth i e (e with e_i deleted). π := ι* := ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint ι.toContinuousLinearMap : ℝ^P → ℝ^{n+1} and π' := ι'* : ℝ^P → ℝ^k likewise. ‖·‖ denotes operator norms; |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_{I strictly increasing} α(b_{I(0)}, …, b_{I(n−1)})²)^{1/2} for an n-covector α on ℝ^P, b_l := EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ l the standard basis of ℝ^P. 1. Adjoint identities. For v ∈ ℝ^{n+1} and w ∈ ℝ^k: π(ιv) = v, π(ι'w) = 0, π'(ι'w) = w and π'(ιv) = 0. Indeed, for every y, ⟨π(ιv), y⟩ = ⟨ιv, ιy⟩ (ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint_inner_left) = ⟨v, y⟩ (LinearIsometry.inner_map_map), and ⟨π(ι'w), y⟩ = ⟨ι'w, ιy⟩ = ⟨ιy, ι'w⟩ = 0 by the orthogonality hypothesis (real_inner_comm); the same computation with the roles of ι and ι' exchanged gives the other two; vectors with the same inner product against every y are equal (ext_inner_right).
2. Norm splitting. For every y ∈ ℝ^P, |y| ≤ |πy| + |π'y|: write y = ιv + ι'w (spanning hypothesis); by step 1, πy = v and π'y = w, and |y| ≤ |ιv| + |ι'w| = |v| + |w|.

Let Θ : ℝ^{n+1} → Λ^n(ℝ^{n+1}) be the continuous linear map Θ := Σ_j (EuclideanSpace.proj j).smulRight β_j, i.e. Θ(z) = Σ_j z_j·β_j. Its affine pull-back P^#α̃ := affinePullbackForm π (−π0) α̃, (P^#α̃)(y) = α̃(−π0 + πy)∘π = α̃(πy)∘π, is a smooth n-form on ℝ^P (affinePullbackForm_isSmoothForm). Let f be the ContDiffBump on ℝ^k centred at 0 with rIn = h and rOut = 2h (0 < h < 2h): f is C^∞ (ContDiffBump.contDiff), 0 ≤ f ≤ 1 (nonneg, le_one), f = 1 on closedBall(0, h) (one_of_mem_closedBall) and support f = ball(0, 2h) (support_eq). If ω(y) ≠ 0 then f(π'y) ≠ 0, so π'y ∈ ball(0, 2h) and |π'y| ≤ 2h; and (P^#α̃)(y) ≠ 0, so φ(πy) ≠ 0 (otherwise α̃(πy) = Θ(0) = 0 and the pull-back vanishes), so πy ∈ tsupport φ. Hence the support of ω lies in Q, and tsupport ω ⊆ Q (closure_minimal). For y ∈ Q, πy ∈ tsupport φ ⊆ ball(0, R) gives |πy| < R, so by step 2 |y| ≤ |πy| + |π'y| < R + 2h. Thus tsupport ω ⊆ Q ⊆ ball(0, R + 2h), which is (i); and tsupport ω is a closed subset of the compact closedBall(0, R + 2h), so ω has compact support. Together with step 5, ω is a test form, and tsupport ω ⊆ univ trivially: ω ∈ TestFormOn univ n.

subproblems.statement: Let m, k, P ∈ ℕ, let ι : ℝ^m → ℝ^P and ι' : ℝ^k → ℝ^P be linear isometries (ℝ^d = Euclid d), b ∈ ℝ^k, R ∈ ℝ, B := ball(0, R) ⊆ ℝ^m, and let β : ℝ^P → Λ^m(ℝ^P) (Covector (Euclid P) m) be continuous with compact support. Let g_i : ℝ^m → ℝ^k (i ∈ ℕ) and let A_i, A ⊆ ℝ^m be measurable sets. Assume (a) L^m((A_i Δ A) ∩ B) → 0 (L^m = Lebesgue measure, Δ = symmetric difference); (b) for all large i, g_i is differentiable at every w ∈ B; (c) for every ε > 0, for all large i, |g_i(w) − b| < ε and ‖Dg_i(w)‖ < ε for all w ∈ B. Put G_i(w) := ιw + ι'g_i(w), DG_i(w) := fderiv ℝ G_i w and e_j := EuclideanSpace.single j 1. Then ∫_{A_i∩B} β(G_i(w))(DG_i(w)e_0, …, DG_i(w)e_{m−1}) dw → ∫_{A∩B} β(ιw + ι'b)(ιe_0, …, ιe_{m−1}) dw as i → ∞ (Bochner integrals with respect to Lebesgue measure on ℝ^m).

Notation. h_i(w) := β(G_i(w))(DG_i(w)e_0, …, DG_i(w)e_{m−1}) and h(w) := β(ιw + ι'b)(ιe_0, …, ιe_{m−1}); L := L^m; |·| Euclidean and operator norms; for u : Fin m → ℝ^P, ‖u‖ := max_j |u_j| (the sup norm, pi_norm_le_iff_of_nonneg).
1. Constants. β is continuous with compact support, hence bounded, |β(y)| ≤ M for all y with some M ≥ 0 (Continuous.bounded_above_of_compact_support), and uniformly continuous (HasCompactSupport.uniformContinuous_of_continuous). B is measurable with L(B) < ∞ (measure_ball_lt_top). |e_j| = 1 and |ιe_j| = 1.
2. The limit integrand. |h(w)| ≤ |β(ιw + ι'b)|·∏_j |ιe_j| ≤ M (ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm), and h is continuous (w ↦ β(ιw + ι'b) is continuous and evaluation at the fixed family ιe is continuous, continuous_eval_const). Hence h is integrable on every set of finite measure (IntegrableOn.of_bound).
3. Derivative of G_i. If g_i is differentiable at w, then DG_i(w) = ι + ι'∘Dg_i(w) (derivative of the linear map ι plus chain rule for ι'∘g_i: HasFDerivAt.add, HasFDerivAt.comp), so DG_i(w)e_j = ιe_j + ι'(Dg_i(w)e_j).
4. Pointwise estimate. Let g_i be differentiable at w with ‖Dg_i(w)‖ ≤ 1; write T := Dg_i(w), y := G_i(w), y' := ιw + ι'b, u_j := DG_i(w)e_j, u'_j := ιe_j. Then |u_j| ≤ |ιe_j| + |ι'(Te_j)| ≤ 1 + ‖T‖ ≤ 2, |u'_j| = 1 and |u_j − u'_j| = |ι'(Te_j)| ≤ ‖T‖; so ‖u‖ ≤ 2, ‖u'‖ ≤ 1 and ‖u − u'‖ ≤ ‖T‖. The second is at most |β(y')|·m·max(‖u‖, ‖u'‖)^{m−1}·‖u − u'‖ ≤ M·m·2^m·‖T‖ (ContinuousAlternatingMap.norm_image_sub_le, 2^{m−1} ≤ 2^m). By (b) and by (c) with δ and with η, for all large i and all w ∈ B: g_i is differentiable at w, |G_i(w) − (ιw + ι'b)| = |ι'(g_i(w) − b)| = |g_i(w) − b| < δ, and ‖Dg_i(w)‖ < η ≤ 1. By step 4, |h_i(w) − h(w)| ≤ 2^m·ε/(2·2^m) + X·ε/(2(X + 1)) ≤ ε/2 + ε/2 = ε. Thus for every ε > 0, for all large i, |h_i − h| ≤ ε on B.
6. Measurability. For every i such that g_i is differentiable on B, h_i is a.e.-strongly measurable with respect to L restricted to B: G_i is continuous at each point of B, hence continuous on B and a.e.-strongly measurable for L⌞B (ContinuousOn.aestronglyMeasurable, B measurable); w ↦ DG_i(w) is measurable for an arbitrary map (measurable_fderiv), hence a.e.-strongly measurable (finite-dimensional target); and h_i(w) = Φ(G_i(w), DG_i(w)) with Φ(y, T) := β(y)(Te_0, …, Te_{m−1}), which is continuous on ℝ^P × L(ℝ^m, ℝ^P) (continuity of β and of T ↦ Te_j, and joint continuity of evaluation, continuous_eval). A continuous function of an a.e.-strongly measurable map is a.e.-strongly measurable. By (b) this holds for all large i.
7. Symmetric differences in ℝ. L((A_i Δ A) ∩ B) → 0 in [0, ∞] by (a), and toReal is continuous at 0 (ENNReal.tendsto_toReal), so the real numbers L((A_i Δ A) ∩ B) tend to 0.
8. Final estimate. Let ε > 0 and V := L(B) ∈ [0, ∞) (as a real number). By steps 5–7, for all large i simultaneously: |h_i − h| ≤ ε/(2(V + 1)) on B, |h_i − h| ≤ 1 on B, h_i is a.e.-strongly measurable for L⌞B, and L((A_i Δ A) ∩ B) < ε/(4(M + 1)). Fix such i and put s := A_i ∩ B, t := A ∩ B (measurable, of finite measure). h_i is integrable on s (a.e.-strongly measurable for L⌞s since s ⊆ B, and |h_i| ≤ |h_i − h| + |h| ≤ 1 + M on s; IntegrableOn.of_bound), and h is integrable on s and on t (step 2). (a) |∫_s h_i − ∫_s h| = |∫_s (h_i − h)| ≤ ε/(2(V + 1))·L(s) ≤ ε/(2(V + 1))·V < ε/2 (integral_sub, norm_setIntegral_le_of_norm_le_const, L(s) ≤ L(B)). (b) ∫_s h = ∫_{s∩t} h + ∫_{s∖t} h and ∫_t h = ∫_{t∩s} h + ∫_{t∖s} h (integral_inter_add_sdiff), so ∫_s h − ∫_t h = ∫_{s∖t} h − ∫_{t∖s} h. A point of s ∖ t lies in B and in A_i but not in A, and a point of t ∖ s lies in B and in A but not in A_i; so both sets lie in (A_i Δ A) ∩ B, and |∫_s h − ∫_t h| ≤ M·L(s∖t) + M·L(t∖s) ≤ 2M·L((A_i Δ A) ∩ B) ≤ 2(M + 1)·ε/(4(M + 1)) = ε/2. subproblems.title: Hausdorff integrals over the image of a measurable set under an affine isometry ℝ^m → ℝ^P (parent Part E)
subproblems.statement: Let m, P ∈ ℕ, let ι : ℝ^m → ℝ^P be a linear isometry (ℝ^d = Euclid d), c ∈ ℝ^P, G(w) := ιw + c, and let A ⊆ ℝ^m be measurable. Then G(A) is a (Borel) measurable subset of ℝ^P, and for every function f : ℝ^P → ℝ, ∫_{G(A)} f dH^m = ∫_A f(G(w)) dw, where H^m = μHE[m] (Mathlib's Euclidean Hausdorff measure) on ℝ^P and dw is Lebesgue measure (volume) on ℝ^m; both sides are Bochner integrals (a non-integrable function has integral 0).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (m P : ℕ) (ι : Euclid m →ₗᵢ[ℝ] Euclid P) (c : Euclid P) (A : Set (Euclid m)), MeasurableSet A → MeasurableSet ((fun w => ι w + c) '' A) ∧ ∀ f : Euclid P → ℝ, ∫ y in (fun w => ι w + c) '' A, f y ∂μHE[m] = ∫ w in A, f (ι w + c)

1. G is an isometry: |G(x) − G(y)| = |ι(x − y)| = |x − y| (Isometry.of_dist_eq, add_sub_add_right_eq_sub, map_sub, LinearIsometry.norm_map). Since ℝ^m is complete, G is a closed embedding (Isometry.isClosedEmbedding), hence a measurable embedding (IsClosedEmbedding.measurableEmbedding). In particular G is injective and G(A) is measurable (MeasurableEmbedding.measurableSet_image').
2. Push-forward. For an isometry, the push-forward of μHE[m] is μHE[m] restricted to the range (Isometry.map_euclideanHausdorffMeasure), and on ℝ^m = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m), μHE[m] = volume (EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume). Hence G_#(volume on ℝ^m) = μHE[m]⌞range G.
3. Restriction. G(A) is measurable and G(A) ⊆ range G, so μHE[m]⌞G(A) = (μHE[m]⌞range G)⌞G(A) (Measure.restrict_restrict; G(A) ∩ range G = G(A)) = (G_#volume)⌞G(A) = G_#(volume⌞G⁻¹(G(A))) (MeasurableEmbedding.restrict_map) = G_#(volume⌞A), because G⁻¹(G(A)) = A by injectivity (preimage_image_eq).
4. Integral. For every f : ℝ^P → ℝ, ∫_{G(A)} f dμHE[m] = ∫ f d(G_#(volume⌞A)) = ∫_A f(G(w)) dw (MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map, which holds for every integrand because G is a measurable embedding). ∎
